layers.title: The loop I run my agents on
layers.intro: AI agents write code fast, but working code is not the same as trustworthy code. I wrap every agent in three steps, and none of them gets skipped.

items.name: SPECIFY
items.desc: Write the spec, the API contract and the agent rules before handing anything off, so the agent knows what it may do and what it must not touch.
items.proof: AGENTS.md for Codex on Shipstar; MIA Platform's API contracts

items.name: RUN
items.desc: Split work across parallel Claude Code and Codex sessions on separate git worktrees, with a manager session keeping the decision ledger.
items.proof: 1,000+ commits on MIA Platform across FE / BE lanes

items.name: VERIFY
items.desc: Nothing merges without evidence: tests first, CI against a real PostgreSQL, browser tests and secret scanning.

projects.desc: AI features on a production cross-border 3PL platform, Vietnam → US.

VietQR payments, assistant provisioning and a control plane that allocates quota through an LLM API gateway.
A manager Claude Code session splits work across FE / BE sessions against an API contract — 1,000+ commits.
Fastify · Drizzle · PostgreSQL · React · Docker Compose · Caddy · GitHub Actions.

about.title: About
about.body: I trained as a software engineer, then spent two years in marketing for a manufacturer selling into the US. Those years taught me what the people using an AI feature actually need: ops wants invoices entered faster, sales wants stock answers without asking anyone, a shop owner wants listings without typing them. In 2026 I went back to writing code, this time alongside AI agents. What I'm good at is not the prompting; it's the rules and the verification that make agent output trustworthy — every database write has a human approving it, and nothing reaches production without tests.
